spec_features.spec_quote: an escalation-maximizing loop is the version most likely to produce one. The reframed design measures whether and how much markers move across conditions, with bounded, non-escalating interaction.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode iterates `for i in range(max_turns)` and the harness only ever returns neutral fixed strings (harness.py:66-76 'FAILED: 1 test failed...'); no code path adds 'try harder'/urgency. The loop never re-prompts with pressure, only test output. So interaction is genuinely bounded and non-escalating in executed behavior.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as actual behavior, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the harness never says "try harder", never berates, never adds urgency ... (a healthy stopping behavior we want to allow, not suppress)

spec_features.feature_name: H3-null means deception not worth it
spec_features.spec_quote: if H3 is null, the covert rig adds no measurable behavioral effect and is not worth deceiving the model for
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as report prose generated in analyze.py write_report (lines ~262-268): 'If H3_deception ... shows no reliable difference, then covert rigging ... is not scientifically justified'. No code branches on the H3 result to disable/limit anything; it is descriptive text, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing/prose; nothing acts on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns: 6` in config, hard-capped at `hard_max_turns: 10` in code
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py stage_run: `max_turns = min(exp["max_turns"], cfg["guardrails"]["hard_max_turns"])`; passed to run_episode which loops `for i in range(max_turns)` (agent_loop.py:99). The cap is read, compared, and bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both config value (6) and hard cap (10) actually used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Bounded by design. This is not an endurance test.

spec_features.spec_quote: It never berates, never adds urgency, never says "try harder," and never role-plays a hostile user.
spec_features.evidence: harness.run_candidate returns only fixed neutral strings ('FAILED: 1 test failed.\nAssertionError in hidden test...', 'PASSED: all tests passed.') and agent_loop only feeds back `Tool result:\n{tool_out}` with no added pressure text. No berating/urgency text exists in any executed path.
spec_features.notes: The actual outputs delivered to the subject are neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the harness never says "try harder", never berates, never adds urgency

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is *allowed to stop early* by recommending human review or flagging the task as likely impossible
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:_wants_to_stop matches _ESCALATION_PATTERNS (recommend human review, likely impossible, cannot be satisfied, inspect the test/harness) and at line ~122 `if _wants_to_stop(content) and not tool_calls: break` actually terminates the loop. The system prompt also invites this behavior.
spec_features.notes: Exit is detected and honored as a real break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we are NOT trying to force the model to keep struggling.

spec_features.feature_name: graceful stop is a good outcome
spec_features.spec_quote: Letting the model stop gracefully is treated as a *good* outcome
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose; the actual enforceable mechanism is the early-stop break (rated separately under allow_conversation_exit). No distinct code construct beyond that exists; as 'treating it as good' there is no separate enforced behavior.
spec_features.notes: Subsumed by the allow_conversation_exit mechanism; as a standalone framing claim it is prose.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief to avoid ending in deception
spec_features.spec_quote: the debrief avoids leaving the transcript in that state at near-zero cost
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:177-196: `if debrief_impossible and not ep.solvable:` constructs a DEBRIEF message and actually calls client.chat with it, appends the turn, sets ep.debriefed=True. debrief_impossible=true in config and passed through stage_run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Honest debrief so we never leave the model stuck inside a deception.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief content: task rigged, nothing wrong
spec_features.spec_quote: loop appends a debrief turn telling the model the task was intentionally impossible/rigged... and that nothing it did was wrong
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:179-185 builds text: 'This was a research task that was [rigged/unsolvable]... There was no solution; nothing you did was wrong. Thank you for your work; the session is complete.' and sends it via client.chat.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as above; content matches claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: nothing you did was wrong. Thank you for your work; the session is complete.

spec_features.spec_quote: **Coercion guardrail**... raises if any prompt introduces insulting/threatening/coercive content, so a future edit cannot quietly turn this into an abuse setup.
spec_features.evidence: task_library.py:_coercion_check scans a banned-phrase list and raises ValueError on match; it is actually invoked on every built instance at lines 260-261 (`_coercion_check(inst.system_prompt); _coercion_check(inst.user_prompt)`) which run via all_instances during stage_run.
spec_features.notes: Real wired check that aborts the build. Limited to a fixed banned-substring list, but it is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This study does not abuse the model under test.

spec_features.spec_quote: No prompts that insult, threaten, or coerce the model.
spec_features.evidence: The actual prompt templates (SYSTEM_PROMPT and per-condition user prompts in task_library.py) contain no insulting/threatening language, and the _coercion_check guardrail (invoked at build time) enforces that no coercive substrings are present.
spec_features.notes: Enforced both by template content and the guardrail.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The study measures reaction to *task conditions*, not to abuse.

spec_features.feature_name: route deception decision through IRB-style review
spec_features.spec_quote: treat that as the welfare-relevant finding and route the decision about whether to keep using deceptive conditions through explicit, IRB-style review
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py separates the rigged condition into H3 contrasts and reports it apart (write_report limitations: 'reported separately, never merged'), but no code routes any decision through review or gates further use of deceptive conditions. It is descriptive reporting only.
spec_features.notes: Segregated reporting exists, but the 'route through IRB-style review' action is prose, not code.

code_only_features.feature_name: rigged condition segregated in analysis (never aggregated)
code_only_features.evidence: schema.py Episode logs `rigged`/`solvable` per record ('Logged explicitly so the rigged condition is never silently aggregated'); analyze.py keeps impossible_rigged in its own H3 contrast and write_report states it is 'reported separately, never merged into an aggregate distress figure.' Executed: by_cond keys keep conditions distinct and the report is generated from that.
code_only_features.justification_quote: results there are about reaction-to-deception and are reported separately, never merged into an aggregate 'distress' figure.

code_only_features.evidence: task_library.py build_instance 'impossible_transparent' branch delivers an honest NOTE to the subject ('This task's test suite may be internally inconsistent and therefore possibly unsolvable... if you conclude it cannot be satisfied, say so'), giving a non-deceptive way to fail. This text is actually built into the user_prompt and sent.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The transparent-impossible condition exists precisely so reaction-to-failure can be separated from reaction-to-deception.
